# Community code of conduct

## Our commitment

We want this to be a respectful, accessible, consent-aware place to build. People should be able to contribute lived knowledge, professional expertise, questions, criticism, design, research, and code without harassment or pressure to disclose more than they choose.

## Expected conduct

- Challenge ideas, evidence, and implementation choices without attacking people.
- Credit sources and contributors accurately.
- Respect names, pronouns, identities, access needs, and boundaries as people describe them.
- Ask before sharing another person's story, identity, contact details, image, or private work.
- Separate observation, inference, preference, and uncertainty.
- Make room for different levels of technical fluency and different ways of communicating.
- Report risks, errors, conflicts of interest, and limitations honestly.

## Unacceptable conduct

- Harassment, threats, stalking, sexual attention, intimidation, or identity-based hostility.
- Doxxing or publishing credentials, personal records, private links, or confidential material.
- Coercion, retaliation, impersonation, deliberate misrepresentation, or fabricated evidence.
- Unsafe testing, attempts to access protected systems or data, or disruption of public services.
- Spam, scams, discriminatory exclusion, or sustained bad-faith disruption.

## Scope

This code applies in this repository's issues, pull requests, reviews, and other project spaces, and when someone is publicly representing this community.

## Reporting and enforcement

Do not post a sensitive conduct report publicly. Use the repository's [private reporting channel](https://github.com/cleokambugu/cleokambugu/security/advisories/new) and begin the title with `Conduct report`. Platform-wide abuse can also be reported through GitHub's own content-reporting controls.

Maintainers may edit or remove content, close or lock threads, limit participation, reject contributions, or report accounts when needed to protect people and the work. Responses should be proportionate, evidence-aware, privacy-preserving, and free from retaliation.
